 2 | |
 3 | | Why this exists
 4 | | ---------------
 5 | | The Stage-2 recovered-only population cannot measure baseline citation
 6 | | recall.  Stage-1 defines ``recovered = retry_hit AND NOT baseline_hit``, so
 7 | | every recovered qid has *no gold chunk in the baseline window*.  And
 8 | |
 9 | |     citation_recall = |cited & gold| / max(|gold|, 1)
10 | |
11 | | is undefined-to-zero when the baseline pool has no gold at all.  On that
12 | | population baseline ``citation_recall`` is structurally 0.00 no matter how
13 | | well the model cites, so SPEC-1's "baseline citation_recall >= 0.50 on the
14 | | 20 paired qids" gate is unachievable by construction.
15 | |
16 | | The population that *can* measure it is the general slice: on all cached
17 | | questions the baseline top-10 window contains gold ~59% of the time
18 | | (Stage-1 ``gold_in_pool.baseline``).  This script selects exactly those
19 | | qids — where the baseline window has gold — and asks the real generation
20 | | path whether the model quotes and cites it.
21 | |
22 | | Population: qids where the baseline top-10 window contains >= 1 gold chunk
23 | | (default 60, i.e. >= 50 per SPEC-1).
24 | |
25 | | Usage:

15 | | difference is whether KG provisions are RRF-fused into the candidate pool):

22 | | difference must appear if the mechanism is real.

 7 | | ``eval_e2e_v2`` scores ``abstain_correct = abstained if insufficient_evidence``.
 8 | | But the evaluator-v2 binary rule is ``token_overlap > 0.5`` against the
 9 | | reference conclusion, and ``abstain_correct`` was never folded in — so answers
10 | | that substantively agree with an abstention-shaped reference ("The available
11 | | corpus … does not establish …") sat at soft 0.27–0.46 and were counted wrong.
12 | |
13 | | Two concrete defects this module repairs, *on the v2 side only*:
14 | |
15 | | 1. ``abstain_correct`` was computed but never applied to ``correct``.
16 | | 2. The v1 abstain lexicon misses common negation phrasings found in the
17 | |    residual answers — e.g. ``cannot be determined`` fails the trailing ``\\b``
18 | |    after ``determine``, and ``does not recognise`` is absent entirely.
19 | |
20 | | Contract
21 | | --------
22 | | * v1 metrics (``answer_correctness`` / ``correct`` / ``abstained``) are the
23 | |   frozen experiment artifacts and are NEVER touched here.
24 | | * ``abstained`` (the reported flag) keeps the v1 regex semantics — only the
25 | |   *credit* path uses the extended lexicon, so no downstream consumer of the
26 | |   abstain flag sees a behaviour change.
27 | | * Per-qid ``banned_abstain_markers`` from the overlay are stripped before
28 | |   matching (Q060/Q138 — reference-matching "does not …" was a false positive).
29 | | * Credit requires ALL of: question is ``insufficient_evidence`` AND the answer
30 | |   matches the extended abstention lexicon AND a non-trivial length (the v1
31 | |   "<20 chars == abstain" heuristic is kept, empty answer too).
32 | | * A substantive answer that never negates (e.g. it enumerates powers the
33 | |   reference says are not established) gets NO credit — the lexicon is
34 | |   deliberately negation-anchored, not "mentions the same subject".
35 | |
36 | | Lexicon location
37 | | ----------------
38 | | The lexicon now lives in ``app.rag.generation.abstention`` and is imported
39 | | here, because ``app/`` must not import from ``evaluation/`` and both sides
40 | | must match the same negation patterns.  One definition, two consumers — the
41 | | locality rule this module already states.  ``ABSTAIN_CREDIT_RE`` is kept as
42 | | this module's public name and is the same object as
43 | | ``app.rag.generation.abstention.ABSTENT_MARKERS_RE``.
44 | |
45 | | The *length* policy intentionally differs between the two consumers and has
46 | | not been changed on either side: this frozen scorer treats any answer under
47 | | ``_MIN_ANSWER_CHARS`` as an abstention, while
48 | | ``app.rag.generation.abstention.is_abstention`` requires a substantive
49 | | statement so that a short degenerate answer is not laundered into
50 | | "not a hallucination".
51 | |
52 | | Deterministic; 0 model calls. Imported by ``rescore_evaluator_v2`` (metric)
53 | | and ``step3_gated_generation`` (before/after scoring) so both sides of every
54 | | comparison use one rule (locality: one home for the lexicon).
55 | | """

 1 | / """P0-1 benchmark: does evidence-set packing change the prompt for the better?
 2 | |
 3 | | Deterministic, offline, no LLM calls.  Uses the cached retrieval arms from

 6 | |
 7 | | What this measures
 8 | | ------------------

10 | | honest question is not "does the prompt look different" (it obviously does) but
11 | | whether the change moves *gold evidence* into a position the model can use.
12 | |
13 | | Two effects are reported per arm:
14 | |
15 | | ``gold_in_prompt``
16 | |     Whether the gold provision's chunk survives into the context at all.
17 | |     Packing must not lose ground here — a role filter that drops gold is a
18 | |     regression even if ordering improves.
19 | |
20 | | ``primary_first``
21 | |     Whether the highest-value provision (primary / subsection / exception)
22 | |     leads the prompt under role ordering.  This is the anti-definition-anchoring
23 | |     claim, and it is the only genuinely new behaviour.
24 | |
25 | | Because the cached arms carry ``chunk_ids`` but not retrieval scores, the
26 | | baseline ordering here is arm order (the cached rank), not re-sorted score.  That

   |
 1 | / """Evaluator v3: can component signals recover the misses a threshold cannot?
 2 | |
 3 | | The 24 ``overlay_insufficient`` cases from ``triage_evaluator_v3`` have already
 4 | | been widened once by v2 and still fail.  This module tests the *other* fix —
 5 | | replace the single token-overlap threshold with per-criterion component credit —
 6 | | and measures whether it separates evaluator misses from genuinely-wrong
 7 | | answers, instead of asserting that it does.
 8 | |
 9 | | Why a threshold cannot work (measured, not assumed)
10 | | ---------------------------------------------------
11 | | Best-arm soft score for unresolved evaluator misses vs ``model_wrong`` answers
12 | | overlaps almost completely (median 0.413 vs 0.379).  Sweeping the threshold
13 | | recovers misses only by also crediting wrong answers; precision peaks near 0.41
14 | | and gets *worse* as the threshold falls.  So the overlap number itself carries
15 | | no separating signal here, and tuning it would move the headline number without
16 | | moving truth.  That is the empirical justification for components.
17 | |
18 | | What this does
19 | | --------------
20 | | Recomputes a v3 verdict per question using signals already available from
21 | | ``grading.grade_answer`` — provision identity (did the answer cite the right
22 | | provision at all?) rather than phrasing overlap.  Reports recovery, false
23 | | credits, and precision so the trade-off is visible.
24 | |
25 | | Usage:
26 | |     python -m evaluation.evaluator_v3_component_rule
27 | |
28 | | Note: this operates on the audit tabulation's recorded machine scores, which do
29 | | not carry per-answer text.  Where a component signal is unavailable it is
30 | | reported as ``unavailable`` rather than silently defaulted — see LIMITATIONS.
31 | | """

 3 | |
 4 | | The registered `reference_narrow` gate forbids spending generation calls and
 5 | | requires dual reporting: "Both the old and the new score are reported until the
 6 | | references are fixed." This module implements the fix-the-reference procedure:
 7 | |
 8 | |   1. --worksheet  write a statute worksheet for the dual-score targets that do
 9 | |                   not yet have a widened conclusion: the v1 reference, the D2
10 | |                   candidate answer, and the O3 evidence anchor (verbatim chunk
11 | |                   text of the primary gold units, cut from the C-manifest O3
12 | |                   payload via the corpus gold index).
13 | |   2. --from-csv   read drafts (question_id, add, note, anchor_quote) filled by
14 | |                   the human from the statute text in the worksheet.
15 | |   3. --validate   mechanical gates per draft (also run inside --merge):
16 | |        - anchor_quote must be a verbatim (whitespace-normalized) substring of
17 | |          the O3 evidence anchor  -> else the qid is evidence_missing, not
18 | |          reference_narrow, and goes back for re-audit;
19 | |        - the widening must NOT paraphrase the stored D2 answer (independence,
20 | |          token_overlap > 0.85) — widening by copying the candidate is scorer
21 | |          gaming and contaminates the 89 non-residual qids' comparability;
22 | |        - the widening must not duplicate the v1 reference (>0.95);
23 | |        - widenings never narrow: v1 text always stays a valid alternative.
24 | |   4. --merge      merge valid drafts into evaluator_v2_overlay.json
25 | |                   (widened_conclusions), additively: existing entries are never
26 | |                   modified or removed. Bumps a 'revisions' provenance record.
27 | |   5. --rescore    rerun evaluation/rescore_evaluator_v2.py (0 LLM calls) so
28 | |                   evaluator_v2_per_question.jsonl carries v1 and v2 side by side.
29 | |   6. --report     write step0_dual_score_report.{json,md}: per-target v1/v2 soft

D301 Use `r"""` if any backslashes in a docstring
  --> kg\enrichment.py:1:1
   |
 1 | / """Corpus-scale semantic enrichment for the legal Knowledge Graph (2026-08-11).
 2 | |
 3 | | Auto-tags every provision with typed legal semantics using deterministic,
 4 | | rule-based pattern matching (no LLM, no external calls):
 5 | |
 6 | | - ``IMPOSES_DUTY``        -> Obligation / Duty concepts   (\"shall\", \"must\", \"duty to\")
 7 | | - ``PROHIBITS``           -> Prohibition concept         (\"shall not\", \"no person shall\", \"prohibited\")
 8 | | - ``CREATES_OFFENCE``     -> Offence concept             (\"offence\", \"punishable\", \"shall be guilty\")
 9 | | - ``PRESCRIBES_PENALTY``  -> Penalty concept             (\"imprisonment\", \"fine\", \"penalty of\")
10 | | - ``GRANTS_POWER_TO``     -> Power concept               (\"may\", \"power to\", \"empowered\")
11 | | - ``GRANTS_PERMISSION``   -> Permission concept          (\"permit\", \"licence\", \"may, subject to\" )
12 | | - ``PRESCRIBES``          -> Procedure concept           (\"procedure\", \"in the prescribed manner\")
13 | |
14 | | Design rules:
15 | |
16 | | 1. **Evidence-backed** — every edge carries the matched sentence fragment as
17 | |    ``evidence`` and a rule-specific ``confidence``, mirroring the audit's
18 | |    D3 requirement (no bare relationship types).
19 | | 2. **Deterministic** — pure regex + priority ordering; re-runs are idempotent
20 | |    (``MERGE``).  No LLM cost, no randomness.
21 | | 3. **Precedence-aware** — \"shall not\" must win over \"shall\" (PROHIBITS beats
22 | |    IMPOSES_DUTY); \"punishable with imprisonment\" wins over bare \"offence\".
23 | | 4. **Targets the typed concept vocabulary** — edges land on the controlled
24 | |    ``LegalConcept`` nodes.  The enricher is standalone, so it calls
25 | |    :meth:`LegalSemanticEnricher.ensure_concepts` to MERGE any vocabulary node
26 | |    it is about to write to.  Without it, ``write_edges``' ``MATCH`` on a
27 | |    concept silently matches nothing and the whole rule group vanishes: the
28 | |    2026-08-11 run reported ``edges_written: 2526`` while 297 of those
29 | |    (DEFINES/EXEMPTS/DECLARES) were dropped on the floor.
30 | | 5. **Honest counters** — ``edges_written`` counts rows Cypher actually
31 | |    materialised (``RETURN count(*)`` after the ``MERGE``), not rows handed to
32 | |    the driver.  A rule group that cannot land must show up as a shortfall,
33 | |    never as a success.
34 | | 6. **Graceful** — provisions with < 40 chars of text (OCR-limited) are skipped
35 | |    (no junk edges from noise); Neo4j absence degrades to an empty report.
36 | |
37 | | The enricher reads provisions + writes edges through the same batched
38 | | ``UNWIND`` MERGE pattern as :class:`kg.corpus_ingestion.KGCorpusIngestionEngine`
39 | | so it runs in minutes on the full 1,861-provision corpus.
40 | | """
   | |___^
41 |
42 |   from __future__ import annotations
   |

 1 | / """Strip spurious ``section_number`` from regulation/notification chunks (G8, 2026-08-17).
 2 | |
 3 | | G8 finding (verified on the 27,351-chunk payload index): 1,518 regulation
 4 | | + 36 notification chunks carry a ``section_number`` that is NOT an Act
 5 | | section — page numbers (``41``, ``01 -``), definition-list numbers, or
 6 | | cross-references in text (``section 23 of Food Safety and Standards Act,
 7 | | 2006``).  They came from the L4 repair regex (``\\d{1,4}\\. [A-Z]``)
 8 | | matching the *first* number on a line, and they pollute section-based
 9 | | matching (``matches_gold``, ``same_section`` mining) with false positives —
10 | | e.g. a regulation fragment stamped ``sec=36`` matches any Act section-36
11 | | gold.
12 | |
13 | | This script deletes ``section_number`` from every chunk whose
14 | | ``document_type`` is regulation/notification/rule (``--document-types``
15 | | configurable).  The identity for those documents is the dotted
16 | | ``clause_number`` (G6/G8), never an Act section — see
17 | | ``scripts/backfill_subsection.py``.  ``rule`` chunks show the same noise
18 | | profile (page numbers, notification numbers, form labels, cross-references
19 | | like ``sub-rule (1) of rule 17`` — verified 2026-08-18: 298 rule chunks), so
20 | | they are stripped by default too.
21 | |
22 | | Payload-only and identity-preserving (same chunk ids, vectors untouched):
23 | | ``set_payload`` with ``{"section_number": None}`` deletes the field in
24 | | Qdrant (null payload values are field deletions), and the DB
25 | | ``metadata_json`` cache mirrors the removal so a future DB-driven re-ingest
26 | | does not resurrect the noise.
27 | |
28 | | Usage:
29 | |     python scripts/strip_reg_section_noise.py                  # dry-run (frozen payload cache)
30 | |     python scripts/strip_reg_section_noise.py --live           # dry-run (scroll Qdrant)
31 | |     python scripts/strip_reg_section_noise.py --apply          # write Qdrant + DB metadata_json
32 | |     python scripts/strip_reg_section_noise.py --apply --no-db  # Qdrant only
33 | |     python scripts/strip_reg_section_noise.py --apply --verify # re-scroll Qdrant and report residue
34 | |     python scripts/strip_reg_section_noise.py --document-types regulation,notification,rule
35 | |
36 | | Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failure, 2 usage/guard error.
